description:
Sizes may be temporarily unavailable as our frame stock sells out. More Montréal frames are currently in production in all sizes, with a tentative ETA of late spring.
Le Montréal, our most popular frameset, is also our most versatile. This build is similar to a classic randonneur bicycle. Randonneuring is, to put it simply, riding fast without racing anybody. It's riding to get somewhere quick, getting out of the city fast to reach the fun gravel roads and wild camping. This bike will do it.
We're building it with road-drop handlebars, which give a lot of hand positions and a more aerodynamic stance, bar-end indexed shifting for reliability that'll last years, and triple gearing to ride up and down every hill. It's easy to add fenders and a front rack for the real randonneur build.
Inspired by classic 1980s touring bikes, Le Montréal features eyelets for front and rear fenders and racks, three bottle cages, and our signature shoulder strap. The wheel size is proportional to the frame size, making the bicycle more comfortable and controllable for variously-sized riders. The stiffened seatstays and top-tube not only increase its load-carrying ability, they also contribute to adding some spring to its step.
A note on pricing: You might notice the 46cm and 61cm are a little cheaper, that's because for the moment, we're still building them with 2022's frames, there's three years of inflation and world economy that happened in between then and now.
Build Specs

Microshift 2x9-speed transmission
Bar-end indexed shifters

Nitto B135AA Randonneur Drop Bars (450mm)

Bassi Classic Compact double crank (46-34t) for a good range of comfortable gears on flat ground as much as in the mountains
Super-tough silver city/touring wheels on polished Sun CR18 rims
Microshift R10 rear derailleur
11-34t Microshift 9-speed Cassette
Panaracer Pasela puncture-resistant all-surface tires, with tan sidewalls for comfort and classic looks
Dia-Compe DC980EX traditional cantilever brakes, great braking power and loads of room for fenders and racks
Bassi Rachel comfort saddle
Tange CDS headset
Bassi quill stem
Cork handlebar tape, with option for cotton
Dia-Compe aero brake levers, black and silver
Bassi frame strap

New features for the Montréal V3

Oversized tubes on all sizes for better stability with a touring load (or your kid) on the rear of the bike
Extra bottle cage mount under the downtube (that's three total)
More rooms for wide tires, up to 45mm on all sizes (with fenders!)
Reduced toe overlap by using three wheel sizes across the range, also making the bicycles more proportional to the rider for more pleasant handling

46cm and 49cm for small riders use 26" wheels
52cm and 55cm for average riders use 650B (27.5") wheels
58cm and 61cm (our largest frame yet!) use 700C (28") wheels

A return to diagonal dropouts, for singlespeed fans

M5 eyelets at mid-fork, on seat stays and drop-outs for rack and fenders
Three bottle cage mounts
Eyelets on seat tube and top tube for shoulder strap
